name: Red Line Extension
gap: CTA’s forecast counts every trip that uses the extension, including bus riders whose routes would be moved to the new stations, park-and-ride at 130th, and the return trip that starts downtown. This tool counts people entering the four new stations with today’s buses, so it comes out much lower.
status: Under construction, opening 2030–31
approx: Follows the route under construction. Station spots: 103rd, 111th, Michigan near 116th and 130th, as CTA gives them.

name: Circle Line (southern half)
status: Studied 2006–09 (this is the first phase); CTA isn’t studying it now. CMAP: “costly for the level of benefits”
approx: CTA’s 2009 preferred route: the Pink Line’s tracks from Ashland/Lake to 18th, with new stations at Congress (Blue Line) and Roosevelt, then about a mile of new elevated track to Cermak/Blue Island and the Orange Line at Ashland. CTA didn’t publish the new track’s exact path; it’s drawn over streets. Trains would continue on the Orange Line’s tracks into the Loop.

official.costNote: year-of-spending dollars, CTA 2009, for the southern phases only; CMAP gives no cost
